notes: Box score from the Utah Jazz's 132–107 road win over the LA Clippers at Intuit Dome on Nov 17, 2026, from the CBS Sports box score and play-by-play, with game details from the Associated Press (via CBS Los Angeles and the Deseret News) and KSL Sports. All 132 Utah points and all 107 Los Angeles points are accounted for in the box score, and the quarter scores (35–23–30–44 to 29–33–24–21) add up to both totals: 62–58 Los Angeles at the half, 88–86 Utah after three. Team totals (threes 20 of 38 to 14 of 37, free throws 14 of 18 to 21 of 27, rebounds 46–31, assists 35–21, steals 7–11, bench points 60–37) are the players' totals in the box score. Biggest leads (Utah 26 at 130–104 with 1:58 left, Los Angeles 4) are from the play-by-play. Records and ranks are from the site's standings after Tuesday's games.

Utah led by 12 early in the second quarter and trailed 62–58 at the half (AP; CBS play-by-play). Rookie Keaton Wagler's three-point play opened the fourth and put the Clippers ahead 89–88; Utah then shot 18 of 22 in the quarter and won it 44–21 (AP). Brice Sensabaugh scored 25 of his 40 in the fourth on 10 of 11 shooting and 5 of 6 from three (AP), and his back-to-back threes at 9:16 and 8:51 made it 103–93 (AP; CBS play-by-play). His 40 were a season high, three short of his career high of 43 (AP; Wikipedia), his 8 threes a career high, and it was his third career 40-point game and second career double-double (KSL Sports). Josh Okogie scored all 9 of his points in the fourth (KSL Sports). The win ended a 12-game losing streak (KSL Sports) and was Utah's first since beating New Orleans on Oct 23; the Jazz had been 0–6 on the road (AP). Lauri Markkanen is out with a right hand injury (KSL Sports). The Clippers had won two straight (AP). Utah plays at the Lakers on Wednesday, Nov 18 (AP; KSL Sports).

The play of the game is an original illustration of Brice Sensabaugh's 3-pointer off a pass from Darryn Peterson with 8:51 left in the fourth quarter, his second three in a row, that made it 103–93 (the CBS play-by-play gives the clock, the score and the assist; AP describes the back-to-back threes). The stories don't describe the shot further, so it is drawn as the template's plain catch-and-shoot three. The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The music is an original beat made for this page. No existing recordings or melodies are used. This is an unofficial fan recap, not affiliated with the Utah Jazz or the NBA, which is why it carries a plain basketball mark and the team's colors but not the team's logo.

The shooter in the play of the game is drawn to Brice Sensabaugh's listed 6-foot-6 and 235 pounds with No. 28 (Wikipedia); no wingspan is reported, so his arms use the standard proportion. He is drawn in Utah's road navy with the default figure (no look on the look sheet yet). It is an original figure with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
